title: Chef Isaac Toups Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
description: A dark-roux chicken and andouille gumbo served over rice.

items.note: or smoked sausage, cut into ½-inch half-moons

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Season the chicken thighs with 2 teaspoons of salt and 1 teaspoon of black pepper. Roast skin-side up on a rimmed baking sheet for 20 minutes, until the skin is lightly browned. Set aside and keep the rendered fat.

In a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat, cook the oil and flour into a dark roux, about 45 minutes, until milk-chocolate colored. Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery and stir about 1 minute until they begin to soften. Add the garlic and bay leaves and cook 30 seconds more.

Deglaze with the beer, scraping up browned bits, and return to a simmer. Add the stock and stir back to a simmer. Add the remaining 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon black pepper, and cayenne. Add the chicken (skin, bones, and fat) and the sausage. Cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 3 hours, stirring every 30 minutes. Thin with a little water if it gets too thick. Do not boil or scorch the roux.
Do not skim the fat off the top.
Serve with rice: gumbo in the bowl first, rice on top. Garnish with sliced green onions and more Louisiana Liquid Snake if you want extra heat.
